title: Bounded session lease for retry-proof metering and exact-cost assignment
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem: At-least-once ingestion and client retries under transient network failures are causing duplicate metering events and overcharges in customer accounts. Existing dedupe heuristics are either too stateful (per-request global stores) or too permissive (short-lived bloom filters) and do not integrate well with rate limiter behavior, resulting in incorrect provisional charges and complicated reconciliation.

Proposal: Introduce a bounded session lease primitive that groups related client retries into a short-lived, server-recognized session. Each session has a lightweight lease token (opaque to customers) and a monotonic local sequence number assigned by the client. The server validates sequence monotonicity per-lease and applies a provisional-reserve / final-commit billing flow for requests in a session. The lease exists for a bounded TTL (default 30s) with an explicit renew path. Leasing enables near-zero state deduping for hot sessions and compact reconciliation for expired sessions. The approach integrates with the token-bucket rate limiter so that retries during transient backpressure are charged once and excess retry attempts are statistically discarded without double-billing.
acceptance_criteria: API: Clients can opt-in to session-lease via new headers: X-RW-Session-Lease (opaque token) and X-RW-Seq (monotonic int)
Billing: Provisional charges are reserved at request acceptance and finalized on commit; duplicate requests within the same lease do not produce additional final charges
Correctness: In canary (10% of traffic) observed per-request duplicate charges drop < 0.001% compared to baseline over a 72h window
Latency: Median request P95 does not regress by more than 3% in canary with lease enabled
Operational: Dashboard shows per-lease dedupe rate, provisional-reserve vs final-commit ratio, and reconciliation outcomes
Rollout: Feature gated, staged canary, automated rollback on anomaly (rate of uncommitted provisional > 1%)
engineering_notes: Lease token: short 128-bit random opaque string issued by ingest frontdoor (or allowed to be client-generated with proof-of-work header). Server keeps only recent active leases in memory with LRU eviction and compact checkpointing to backing store for longer reconciliation windows.

Sequence enforcement: server enforces non-decreasing X-RW-Seq per-lease; out-of-order sequences are NACKed with suggested retry-after when possible. Duplicate sequence numbers are treated as idempotent replays and map to previous response if available.

Billing flow: request accepted -> provisional reservation record (small, cheap) -> work executed -> final commit marks reservation consumed. If commit does not arrive within lease TTL + grace window, a reconciliation job either credits or finalizes based on logs.

Rate limiter interaction: use a cross-check where provisional reservations decrement token-bucket capacity immediately to avoid burst double-reservation. If reservation fails due to limit, client should get 429 and can retry with the same lease token but will not produce duplicate provisional charges.

State size constraints: keep per-lease metadata limited to 128 bytes (lease id, last_seq, provisional_count, checksum of last response). Use periodic compaction to coalesce long-lived leases into a single reconciliation marker to avoid indefinite growth.
Storage/backing: provisional reservations are appended to the fast append-only ledger (sharded by customer) with tombstones for final commits. The ledger is compacted by lease id sweeps.

Reconciliation: async sweeper runs reconciliation based on ledger age; if final commit missing after reconciliation threshold, either charge or credit per policy flag on customer account (default: credit after 7 days).
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Problem statement and proposal drafted (this ticket). Added initial acceptance criteria and labels.

2026-03-11: Architecture sync with infra and billing teams. Agreed to use append-only provisional ledger and to bound lease TTL to 30s by default. Action: infra to prototype fast in-memory lease cache with eviction metrics (PR #4723).

2026-03-12: Implemented minimal client SDK change to emit X-RW-Seq when lease header present. Local e2e tests show dedupe for simple retry loop. Opened prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4745
2026-03-13: Canary rollout plan drafted and signed off by PM (Kai Morgan). Created dashboard draft: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/ledger/lease-dedupe?orgId=1
2026-03-13: Requested security review for lease token handling and potential replay amplification (security ticket SEC-882).
testing_plan: Unit tests for seq monotonicity and duplicate detection (server): target 100% branch coverage on enforcement codepaths
Integration tests: simulate client retry storms + token-bucket backpressure to validate no double final charges
Chaos tests: introduce random lease eviction to exercise reconciliation and credit-flow path
Load test: 10k leases/s for 1h in staging to validate memory bounds and compaction logic
Billing regression: run historical-sim replay against 7-day window to estimate impact on outstanding provisional reservations
rollout_plan: Internal canary (10%): enable for a small set of high-usage developer orgs, monitor dedupe and provisional ratios
Expand canary to 30% after 48h of stable metrics and no billing anomalies
Gradually roll to 100% after two full days of stable behavior and audit sign-off
Automated rollback if provisional_to_final ratio > 1% sustained for 30m or customer-facing errors increase
blockers: Need infra PR (#4723) to finalize in-memory lease cache with eviction hooks
Security review (SEC-882) outstanding: concerns around client-generated lease tokens and replay amplification
Billing team needs confirmation on default reconciliation policy for uncommitted provisional reservations
audit_log_strategy: Emit per-lease append-only events to ledger with minimal PII. Events: lease-issued, provisional-reserve, final-commit, lease-expired, reconciliation-action. Keep 90d retention for high-importance customers and 30d baseline.
